content.text: No minimum purchase, take-or-pay, shortfall, or volume-cap obligation exists anywhere in the Agreement. Supply from Array is expressed as Ono's right, payments are transfer-price-per-order and sales-based royalties.

input.quote: (b) Without limiting the foregoing, Ono shall have the right to obtain from Array Ono's commercial requirements of Materials for the Ono Territory.
input.rationale: The Agreement imposes no minimum purchase, take-or-pay, shortfall or volume commitment on Ono, so it sits at the preferred position. Article IX frames supply entirely as Ono's entitlement: Array must supply "Ono's requirements" (9.1(a)), clinical Materials are procured only "as reasonably requested in writing by Ono" (9.3(a)), and commercially Ono "shall have the right to obtain from Array Ono's commercial requirements" (9.4(b)) while also having "the right (but not the obligation) to Manufacture" or source those requirements itself (9.4(a)). Payments are consumption-based only: transfer price for Materials actually ordered, and royalties calculated on Annual Net Sales (Section 6.3) with no minimum annual royalty. The future clinical and commercial supply agreements will contain "forecasting and ordering procedures" (9.3(a), 9.4(b)(i)), which is the usual home for binding-forecast exposure, but those are agreements-to-agree on commercially reasonable terms and create no present commitment; we would police any binding forecast when those documents are negotiated. No redline is warranted.
